narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Ninety degrees is the largest acute angle, because it is the biggest one before obtuse.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Look at six gaps of the big wheel. They make a right angle, with the small square mark.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>A right angle is not acute. An acute angle must be smaller than that.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble says ninety degrees is the largest acute angle; six gaps of the big wheel are shaded and a small square mark shows the angle is a right angle; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, count all twenty four gaps of fifteen degrees and see that they fill the full turn.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Then check that five gaps are less than a right angle, and six gaps are not.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the recap board shows the check: 24 gaps of 15° make 360°, and 5 gaps of 15° make 75°

old_misconception.wrong_answer: ninety degrees is the largest acute angle
old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu says ninety degrees is the largest acute angle, because six gaps make exactly ninety degrees. Ninety degrees is a right angle, and an acute angle must be smaller, so the bubble is struck.
